faqs.q: What paperwork does a Freetown import of hydraulic parts need from Dubai?
faqs.a: Three items gate the shipment: pre-shipment inspection of regulated goods by the appointed inspection body before the vessel sails, an import licence where the product requires one, raised by the consignee with the ministry, and a Dubai Chamber attested Certificate of Origin. The bill of lading and packing list follow on loading, and material and test certificates are added where the order calls for them.

faqs.q: Does every product shipped to Sierra Leone need an import licence?
faqs.a: No. Some products need one and most do not, and we confirm at quotation which lines on your list are affected. Where a licence applies, the consignee raises it with the ministry before shipment, so it is worth flagging early: the container does not load until the licence is in hand, and a late licence costs a sailing rather than a day.

faqs.q: Are Sierra Leone shipping documents prepared in English?
faqs.a: Yes. Sierra Leone clears on English-language documentation, which keeps this lane simpler than the francophone lanes into neighbouring Guinea and the Sahel, where invoices and packing lists must be in French. Our commercial invoice, packing list, Certificate of Origin and any test certificates are issued in English and matched to the inspection before the vessel sails.

faqs.q: Why is Freetown four to five weeks from Jebel Ali by sea?
faqs.a: Because the routing runs around the Cape of Good Hope. FCL typically takes 30–36 days from dispatch; consolidated LCL, with transshipment, runs 36–44 days and suits small mixed orders. When a line is down, air freight from DXB into Lungi (FNA) takes six to eight days and is quoted per shipment, so the cost can be weighed against the downtime.

faqs.q: Should equipment for Sierra Leone land at Freetown or at Pepel?
faqs.a: Freetown is the default port of entry for general cargo and for CIF terms. Pepel, across the estuary, serves the bulk terminals, so it is worth naming when the equipment is for ore-handling plant there. Tell us where the goods are finally needed and we quote the port that gives the shorter, simpler last leg rather than defaulting to one.

faqs.q: Which mining spares do you ship for Sierra Leone's iron ore, rutile and diamond operations?
faqs.a: Slurry valves, four-spiral hose, high-cycle cylinders and crusher-duty components make up most of the volume. Iron ore around Marampa and Tonkolili wears hose and cylinders on loaders and haul trucks; rutile operations in the south need slurry valves and abrasion-resistant hose; diamond processing at Koidu runs crusher and screen hydraulics. Material certificates are supplied where the contract calls for them.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to the mine gate at Koidu, Marampa or Kabala?
faqs.a: Yes, on DAP terms to the site gate. The inland leg from Freetown is quoted rather than estimated, because Koidu and Kabala are a long way from the quay. Give us the site name and the receiving contact at quotation, and the inland transport is priced and documented alongside the sea freight, so one quotation covers Jebel Ali to the mine.

faqs.q: Do hose assemblies for Sierra Leone arrive crimped and pressure-tested?
faqs.a: Yes. Assemblies are crimped and pressure-tested in our Dubai bay and shipped as finished items, tagged with the hose, the fittings and the test date. Where a site has no crimping capability it can rely on, a finished assembly is a safer purchase than bulk hose and loose ends. Send lengths and end configurations, or the old assembly, and the tag lets the next one be reordered by reference.

faqs.q: Can you supply wire rope slings to length for Sierra Leone's ore terminals and mine workshops?
faqs.a: Yes. Wire rope and chain slings are supplied to the length, leg count and working load limit you specify, with shackles, hooks and master links, each marked with its working load limit and shipped with its test certificate. For ore handling at Pepel or workshops inland, give us the load, the sling angle and the hook arrangement and we propose the assembly.

faqs.q: How do I request a quotation for delivery to Freetown or a Sierra Leone mine site?
faqs.a: Send the part list, photographs or old assemblies, quantities and the delivery point — Freetown, Pepel or a named site. We reply with a quotation in USD on CIF Freetown, DAP to site, FOB Jebel Ali or EXW Dubai, and confirm which lines need inspection or an import licence. Once accepted, inspection and the shipping documents are arranged before the container is loaded.

faqs.q: Can you supply contractors on the Greater Tortue Ahmeyim gas project off Mauritania?

faqs.q: Can you deliver DAP to Zouerate, Tasiast or Akjoujt?

faqs.q: Why does sea freight from Dubai to Nouakchott take over a month?
faqs.a: Because the routing runs around the Cape of Good Hope: typically 30–38 days by FCL from dispatch to Nouakchott, and 32–40 days to Nouadhibou. faqs.q: How do you protect hose assemblies against dust on Mauritanian mine sites?

faqs.q: Which rigging hardware stands up to salt air at Nouadhibou?

faqs.q: Do you supply the Nouadhibou fishing fleet and fish-processing plants?

Vessel spares can ship by sea to Nouadhibou directly, with verification and the French documents arranged before the vessel sails.

faqs.q: How far ahead should a Mauritanian site order planned maintenance spares?
faqs.a: Plan backwards from the shutdown: 30–40 days of sea freight, plus the time to complete pre-shipment verification and the import declaration before the vessel sails, plus the inland leg to site. faqs.q: What makes the Dubai–Bamako lane longer than a coastal delivery?
faqs.a: The lane has two long halves: four to five weeks by sea around the Cape to Dakar, then about twelve hundred kilometres of corridor through Diboli to Bamako. Door to door is typically 35–45 days, or 38–48 via Abidjan. For anything that is not urgent, that is the argument for consolidating maintenance buying into fewer, complete consignments.

faqs.q: When does Abidjan beat Dakar as the gateway for Malian cargo?
faqs.a: Dakar suits most orders and is the default routing. Abidjan, typically 38–48 days via the northern corridor, is the alternative when the delivery is in the south — around Sikasso, Bougouni or Syama — or when the Dakar corridor is congested. On orders large enough for the difference to matter, we quote both routings side by side.

faqs.q: Which documents does a consignment need to clear at Dakar and Diboli?
faqs.a: It clears twice, as Senegalese transit at Dakar and as a Malian import at Diboli, so the paperwork must satisfy both before loading. The consignee lodges the import declaration through the bank before the vessel sails; regulated lines are verified in Dubai by the appointed inspection body; the nominated forwarder raises the Senegalese transit documents; and we issue the French invoice, packing list and Dubai Chamber attested Certificate of Origin.

faqs.q: Do you deliver to the mine gates at Sadiola, Loulo and Syama?
faqs.a: Yes, on DAP terms to the mine gate. Sadiola and Loulo are in Kayes Region in the west, nearer the Dakar corridor, while Syama is in Sikasso Region in the south, where the Abidjan routing is worth quoting. Either way the final leg is quoted rather than estimated. Give us the site and the receiving contact, and the inland transport is priced with the freight.

faqs.q: Which spares do you ship for gold processing in Mali?
faqs.a: Slurry valves, four-spiral hose, high-cycle cylinders and crusher-duty components for pits, crushers and processing plant, with material certificates where the contract calls for them. Because the sites are landlocked, remote and dusty, filtration elements, caps and clean decanting equipment are worth adding to the same consignment: on this lane the cheapest freight is the line that travels with the main order.

faqs.q: How do you keep hydraulic fluid clean on dusty Malian mine sites?
faqs.a: Most pump and valve failures there start as particulate contamination, not a wrong specification. We supply filtration against ISO 4406 cleanliness targets and will advise on the code your system actually needs, ship assemblies capped at both ends, and can include decanting and breather equipment. Fitting dust caps at every coupling break and on every stored assembly costs little compared with a seized pump.

faqs.q: When should a Malian site pay for air freight into Bamako?
faqs.a: When the plant is down. Air freight from DXB into Bamako (BKO) takes five to seven days against 35–45 days by sea and road, and is quoted per shipment. For a planned order the sea and road lane costs a fraction of it, so the usual pattern is one consolidated sea consignment with only the critical line flown.

faqs.q: Do assemblies for Mali ship finished and tested, or as bulk hose and fittings?
faqs.a: Finished. Assemblies are crimped and pressure-tested in Dubai and shipped tagged with the hose, the fittings and the test date, capped against dust. A crimp is only as good as the die, the diameter and the calibration behind it, so on a remote site in western Mali a tested assembly is the safer purchase. Send lengths and end types, or the old assembly.

faqs.q: Can you supply gate and governor hydraulics for Manantali and Sélingué?
faqs.a: Yes. We supply gate operator cylinders, governor and actuator hydraulics, hose assemblies and valves for hydropower plant, matched to the existing nameplate data or drawings. Manantali is in Kayes Region and Sélingué is south-west of Bamako, so both are served on the normal corridor with the final leg quoted on DAP terms. Material and test certificates are supplied where the order calls for them.

faqs.q: How should a Bamako buyer or mine site request a quotation?
faqs.a: Send a complete part list, photographs or old assemblies, quantities and the delivery point — Bamako, a mine gate, or CIF Dakar. We quote in USD on DAP Bamako or site, CIF Dakar, FOB Jebel Ali or EXW Dubai. A complete list matters more here than on a short lane, because once verification and both sets of transit documents are raised, an amendment costs weeks.

faqs.q: What paperwork does a Chad consignment need at Douala and at the Kousseri border?
faqs.a: Four sets, prepared before the container is loaded: pre-shipment verification for regulated goods by the appointed inspection body before the vessel sails; Cameroonian transit documents for the corridor leg, raised by the nominated forwarder at Douala; the invoice and packing list in French; and a Certificate of Origin attested by the Dubai Chamber. Material and test certificates travel too where the order calls for them. The goods clear as Cameroonian transit at Douala and as a Chadian import at the border.

faqs.q: Why does Dubai to N’Djamena take six to eight weeks by sea?
faqs.a: Because the sea leg is only part of the journey. It is four to five weeks by sea around the Cape to Douala, then about nineteen hundred kilometres of road north-east through Cameroon to Kousseri and N’Djamena — typically 40–55 days in all. The road leg, not the ocean, is what moves the delivery date, which is why we quote that leg rather than estimate it.

faqs.q: When does air freight into N’Djamena make sense instead of the Douala corridor?
faqs.a: More often than on any other African lane. Air freight from Dubai into N’Djamena runs six to nine days against 40–55 days by sea and road, so for a stopped pump, a failed hose on a rig or a small high-value order, the downtime saved usually outweighs the freight cost. We quote both modes side by side so the decision is made on numbers rather than habit.

faqs.q: How does the rainy season change delivery times to Chad?
faqs.a: It lengthens the road leg. Corridor restrictions in the rainy season can push sea-and-road delivery from 40–55 days to 55–70 days — two weeks or more on top of the normal band. We quote the road leg for the period the goods will actually travel rather than averaging it, and for anything time-critical in that window we quote air freight into N’Djamena alongside.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to the Doba oilfields and the camps around Komé?
faqs.a: Yes, on DAP terms to the site gate. The final leg south to Doba, Komé or Moundou is quoted per consignment rather than estimated, and site access requirements need to come with the order. Pre-shipment verification and the French document set are completed before dispatch, so nothing has to be corrected at the border while a field crew waits for the parts.

faqs.q: Why must the French invoice match the Cameroonian transit documents?
faqs.a: Because the goods are checked twice against them. The transit file raised at Douala and the Chadian import declaration at the border both read from the same invoice and packing list, which we prepare in French before dispatch. A description, quantity or weight that differs between the two is the usual reason a container stands still on this corridor, so we build both from one source.

faqs.q: How do you pack hose and fittings for the long road leg to Chad?
faqs.a: For the road rather than the ship. A thousand kilometres and more of vibration works threads loose and shifts unsupported weight, so for Chad we crate rather than carton, coil hose assemblies to their minimum bend radius instead of however they fit, and protect threads and sealing faces individually. It costs a little more at dispatch and far less than a consignment that arrives complete but unusable.

faqs.q: Can you send hose assemblies ready to fit, so nothing has to be crimped in N’Djamena?
faqs.a: Yes. Hydraulic and industrial hose assemblies are made up to length, crimped and pressure-tested in Dubai, tagged with the hose, fittings and test date, and crated for the road. Send the length, end fittings and working pressure, or the part number from the old hose, and we build to it — which matters in Chad, where a failed assembly far from a workshop otherwise means a long wait.

faqs.q: Which standards do hydraulic and oilfield orders for Chad follow?
faqs.a: Whatever the specification calls for. Hydraulic hose to SAE J517 and EN 853/856, fittings in BSP, JIC, NPT, metric and ORFS, and wellsite items to API specifications such as API 6A, with material and test certificates from the mill or our test bench where the order requires them. We supply TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM equipment for wellhead and flow-iron requirements.

faqs.q: Should we combine several requisitions into one shipment to Chad?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. There is no minimum on stock items, but this is the lane where consolidation saves the most: one container, one verification, one transit file and one corridor movement instead of several. Send the requisitions together and we quote them as a single consignment, with anything urgent split out for air freight into N’Djamena so it is not held back by the road leg.

faqs.q: How do we get a quotation for delivery to N’Djamena?
faqs.a: Send the RFQ with part numbers or descriptions, quantities, the delivery point and how urgent it is. We reply with a USD quotation showing the terms that fit — DAP N’Djamena or your site, CIF Douala, FOB Jebel Ali, or EXW Dubai for your own forwarder — with sea-and-road and air freight priced separately and the French document set and verification requirements noted.

faqs.q: Why does Armenia need EAC documents when Georgia, on the same corridor, does not?
faqs.a: Because Armenia is a member of the Eurasian Economic Union and Georgia is not. The EAC declaration or certificate of conformity applies to Armenian imports and is raised by an accredited body in the importer’s name before anything else moves — the same framework Kazakhstan works under. Georgia needs none of it. Because the two countries share the same corridor and the same port, getting this backwards is the commonest error on this lane.

faqs.q: Why is Poti and Sadakhlo the only route you quote into Armenia?
faqs.a: Because it is the only usable one. Two of Armenia’s four land borders are closed, and the alternatives either cross jurisdictions we will not route through without an export-compliance ruling or are not commercially served. Cargo sails from Jebel Ali through Suez to Poti and comes south by road through the Sadakhlo–Bagratashen crossing. Quoting an option we would not actually use would be worse than admitting there is one road.

faqs.q: What transit should a Yerevan buyer plan around?
faqs.a: Typically 26–34 days from dispatch for sea to Poti and road south, and 32–42 days for a small mixed order consolidated to Poti before the road leg. Air freight from Dubai to Yerevan takes 3–5 days and is the answer when a line is down. The sea time to Poti is predictable; the Georgian transit clearance, the drive south and the border at Bagratashen make up the rest of the figure.

faqs.q: Why does a shipment to Armenia take longer than one to Georgia?
faqs.a: Because it is the Georgian lane plus a road leg and a second customs file. The sea time to Poti is identical. The difference is the Georgian transit documents for the road leg, the drive south to the border and the Armenian entry at Bagratashen. That is why the transit documents are prepared alongside the EAC file before the vessel sails, rather than started once the container is already standing at Poti.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to the Syunik mines at Kajaran and Kapan?
faqs.a: Yes, on DAP terms to the mine gate at Kajaran or Kapan. It is a long road leg south from the Bagratashen border through the length of the country, so it is quoted rather than estimated. For shovel, haul-truck and mill hydraulics, send the machine model and the position along with the part number or a photograph, so assemblies arrive ready to fit rather than needing rework at a remote site.

faqs.q: What must be in place before goods leave Dubai for Armenia?
faqs.a: Confirmation that the EAC documentation is in place in your name and covers the goods — it cannot be arranged after arrival. We also need the delivery address, so the Georgian transit documents for the road leg match the destination, and the importer details for the customs declaration. With those settled the file is complete before the vessel sails, and you receive the paperwork and the tracking together.

faqs.q: Can goods for Armenia clear customs in Georgia instead?
faqs.a: No. Goods bound for Armenia cross Georgia under transit documents prepared by the forwarder at Poti, and the import entry is made in Armenia. Clearing them into Georgia would put them into the wrong customs territory — Georgia is outside the Eurasian Economic Union — and the EAC file raised for the Armenian importer would no longer match the consignment. Tell us at enquiry that Armenia is the destination, so the file is built for it.

faqs.q: Should an Armenian buyer purchase CIF Poti or DAP to site?
faqs.a: DAP to your site if you want one party responsible through the Georgian transit and the road south; CIF Poti if you have a forwarder who already runs the road leg and the border at Bagratashen. Either way the EAC documentation must be in your name before the goods move. FOB Jebel Ali and EXW Dubai for a nominated forwarder are also available on this lane.

faqs.q: What does the importer lodge with the State Revenue Committee?
faqs.a: The customs import declaration, lodged by the importer through the State Revenue Committee before the goods arrive at the border. It sits alongside the EAC documents in your name. We supply what it is built from: commercial invoice and packing list, a Dubai Chamber attested certificate of origin, and material and test certificates from the mill or our test bench where the order calls for them. Descriptions match across every document.

faqs.q: Can urgent parts go by air to Yerevan while the rest of the order travels by sea?
faqs.a: Yes. The item that is stopping a machine can fly from Dubai to Yerevan in 3–5 days while the balance travels by sea to Poti and road south, typically 26–34 days. Both parts of the order still need EAC documentation that covers the goods, raised in your name, so tell us at quotation which lines are urgent and we split the consignment and its documents from the start.

faqs.q: Should cargo for Georgia go to Poti or Batumi?

Batumi serves Adjara and the south-west, while Poti sits closer to Kutaisi, Zestaponi and the main road east to Tbilisi and Rustavi. faqs.q: Why does Georgian cargo go through Suez rather than overland from the Gulf?

faqs.q: Can cargo landing at Poti continue to Armenia, Baku or Aktau?

faqs.q: What transfer hose do you supply for Black Sea oil terminals?

Flexible sections on a loading system are inspected and certified as part of it, and they carry hydrocarbons at volume, where a failure is an environmental event. Composite construction is common for that reason — it fails progressively rather than catastrophically. Tell us the product and the certification regime, and we work within both.

faqs.q: What hose survives furnace-side duty at Zestaponi and Rustavi?
faqs.a: Hose protected for the heat it actually sees, routed so it is not the first thing radiant heat reaches. Near ferroalloy furnaces and hot metal lines we specify heat-resistant sleeving over the assembly, fittings in a material suited to the temperature, and a working-pressure margin that allows for heat ageing. Tell us the distance from the heat source, the fluid and its temperature, and the position in the circuit, and we specify from that.

faqs.q: Does air freight into Tbilisi make sense for planned maintenance?
faqs.a: Usually not. Air from Dubai to Tbilisi takes three to five days and is worth its cost when a line is down; for planned work the sea lane to Poti, typically 22–28 days, is predictable enough to order against. What we are asked for is the pattern that is not held locally: GOST couplings for a Central Asian contract, SS316L thread forms and API-monogrammed assemblies. Locally that is often a six-week factory order; for us it is stock, ten to fourteen days by sea to Mersin or two to four days by air to Istanbul.

faqs.q: When does a hose assembly shipped to Türkiye need CE marking?
faqs.a: When it sits above the pressure-volume threshold in PED 2014/68/EU. A hydraulic hose assembly is a pressure accessory: above the threshold it needs a declaration of conformity travelling with the goods; below it, the directive requires sound engineering practice and no CE mark at all. Suppliers who CE-mark everything and suppliers who mark nothing are both wrong, so we state which side of the line each item sits on at quotation.

faqs.q: Who issues the PED declaration of conformity — you or the hose maker?
faqs.a: We do, as the assembler, for assemblies above the PED threshold. The assembly is the pressure accessory, not the bulk hose or the loose fitting, so the declaration belongs to whoever makes the assembly up. It is issued before dispatch and travels with the goods to Mersin, Ambarlı or Izmir. Material and test certificates from the mill or our test bench are added where the order calls for them.

faqs.q: Does industrial hose need TSE conformity in Türkiye?
faqs.a: Only where the line is on the Turkish Standards Institution’s defined list of regulated products. Much industrial hose and many fittings sit outside it. Where a line is inside, the assessment is arranged before shipment and settled per product at quotation, so it never surfaces for the first time at Turkish Customs. The importer raises the customs import declaration before arrival, against our invoice and attested certificate of origin.

faqs.q: Mersin, Ambarlı, Gemlik or Izmir — which port suits our plant?
faqs.a: Mersin for the southern and south-eastern belt — Adana, Iskenderun, Gaziantep. Ambarlı or Gemlik for Marmara — Istanbul, the Izmit and Gebze industrial zones in Kocaeli, and Bursa. Izmir for the Aegean — Manisa and Aliağa. The road leg across Anatolia is long enough that choosing the port is worth the minute it takes, rather than defaulting to Mersin and trucking the container north.

faqs.q: Can a Turkish contractor’s site in Iraq or Central Asia receive API equipment direct from Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes, with the commercial relationship kept in Türkiye. API 6A wellhead, API 16A BOP, API 16C choke and kill and API 7K drilling hose ship to the site with NACE MR0175 documentation where the contract requires it. We supply TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM equipment. From Dubai, those sites are usually closer and simpler to reach than from Istanbul.

faqs.q: Can you supply GOST-pattern couplings for a contract in Kazakhstan or Turkmenistan?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is one of the commoner reasons Turkish buyers call us. We hold GOST-pattern couplings and adapters alongside the DIN, BSP, JIC and ORFS ranges, so a contract that mixes Soviet-standard plant with European machinery ships from one order. The goods can come to Türkiye first or go straight to the project, depending on where the contract and its documentation sit.

faqs.q: Can one agreement in Istanbul cover deliveries to several countries?
faqs.a: Yes. A contractor can hold one agreement and one set of terms with us in Türkiye and take deliveries wherever the work is — Kazakhstan, Iraq or Libya are markets we ship to routinely. It also solves the interchangeability problem a contractor accumulates when each site buys locally, because the same specification arrives everywhere instead of five near-equivalents that do not swap between sites.

faqs.q: Which stainless thread forms are worth importing rather than ordering from a Turkish factory?
faqs.a: The SS316L patterns a local factory makes to order rather than holds. When an offshore, chemical or food specification calls for stainless in a thread form or seat that is not stocked domestically, the local route is often a six-week factory order while ours is stock. Send the thread form, size, pressure and the standard named in the specification, and we confirm what is held at quotation.

faqs.a: Yes, for the hydraulic and utility circuits on the plant — valve actuators, governor and control hydraulics, and transfer lines — specified from the medium and its temperature. Geothermal fluid is hot and often corrosive, so the hose, liner and fitting material are chosen from what the line actually carries. Tell us the fluid, temperature and pressure, and whether the assembly sits near brine or steam piping.

Most hose and fittings sit outside the TISI regulated list, so classification, not a certificate, is what keeps a consignment moving. From Laem Chabang the Rayong, Map Ta Phut and Chonburi estates are a short road leg, and production lines get the same construction every time.

faqs.q: What is TISI and does it cover hydraulic hose and fittings?
faqs.a: TISI is the Thai Industrial Standards Institute, which regulates a defined list of products, and most hydraulic hose, fittings, adapters and valves are not on it. Send the part list at quotation and we will say which lines, if any, are in scope rather than certifying everything to be safe. Where a line genuinely falls on the list, the certification is arranged at origin before the container is loaded.

faqs.q: Should we ship to Laem Chabang or Bangkok Port?
faqs.a: Laem Chabang if you are on the eastern seaboard, as most industrial buyers are: it is deeper, busier and close to Chonburi, Rayong and Map Ta Phut. Bangkok Port suits a delivery in the city or the central plain, such as Ayutthaya or Samut Prakan. Songkhla serves the south. Name the delivery estate at quotation and we will price the port that fits it.

faqs.q: What holds a hydraulic consignment at Thai customs?
faqs.a: Almost always the tariff classification. Thai customs query a description that does not sit comfortably with the declared code, and a queried consignment waits at the port while it is resolved. We fix the classification line by line at quotation and state it on the invoice, so your broker declares what we shipped rather than what he guesses we shipped. That one step removes the most common cause of delay on this lane.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to plants at Map Ta Phut, Rayong or Chonburi?
faqs.a: Yes, on DAP terms to the plant gate. The eastern seaboard estates are a short road leg from Laem Chabang, and that leg is priced at quotation rather than estimated. For refinery and petrochemical sites at Map Ta Phut, tell us the gate-entry and delivery-window rules at enquiry, so the truck arrives when the stores can receive it and the goods are not turned away at the gate.

faqs.q: Do you provide NACE sour-service documentation for Thai refinery and gas work?
faqs.a: Yes. NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 material documentation is supplied where the contract requires it, stated at quotation and shipped with the goods rather than produced after the fact. That matters for valves, flow iron and wellhead parts going into sour gas or refinery service, where an inspector will ask for the material record before the item is accepted, not after it is installed.

faqs.q: Will replacement assemblies for our production line match the originals exactly?
faqs.a: That is how we supply them. On a line validated to fixed cycle times, a hose with a different wall stiffness or a fitting with a slightly different bore can put it out of tolerance even when the part is nominally better. We crimp assemblies in Dubai, pressure-test and tag them, and supply the same construction from the same source each time; where a product has to change, we tell you before shipping.

faqs.q: How many days does a shipment from Jebel Ali to Laem Chabang take?
faqs.a: Typically 18–24 days from dispatch for a full container on the sea route round the peninsula. Small mixed orders shipped LCL are consolidated with transhipment and take 24–32 days. Air freight from DXB to BKK takes 3–5 days. Because most hose and fittings need no TISI certificate, the freight time is close to the whole lead time once the classification is settled.

faqs.q: Can you ship to Songkhla for Gulf of Thailand offshore work?
faqs.a: Yes. Songkhla serves the south and the offshore supply operations for the Gulf of Thailand fields, and we quote it as a destination port in its own right rather than routing everything through Laem Chabang. Give us the vessel or campaign date and the base the goods are for, and we will plan the sailing back from it and pack by vessel or platform where needed.

faqs.q: Do you supply wellhead equipment and flow iron for the Gulf of Thailand gas fields?
faqs.a: Yes. We supply TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM equipment, so wellhead components, valves and flow iron for fields such as Erawan and Bongkot can be quoted alongside hydraulic hose on one consignment. Pressure rating, material class and the certificates the contract calls for, including sour-service documentation, are confirmed per line at quotation.

faqs.q: Can you supply cement plants and quarries in Saraburi?
faqs.a: Yes. Saraburi and the central plain are served through Bangkok Port, with delivery to the plant on DAP terms priced at quotation. Kiln, crusher and loader hydraulics in cement and quarry service run hot, dusty and continuous, so we specify hose cover, fittings and seals for abrasion, heat and cycle life as well as pressure, and supply the same construction on each reorder.

faqs.q: Do you supply slings, shackles and lifting gear to Thailand?
faqs.a: Yes. Wire rope and chain slings, shackles, hooks and rigging hardware ship from Dubai marked with their working load limit and with the manufacturer’s test certificates the order calls for, on the same consignment as hydraulic parts. Whether a lifting line falls on the TISI list is confirmed from the part list at quotation. Inspection on site stays with your appointed lifting inspector.

faqs.q: What should a Thai enquiry include to avoid questions at clearance?
faqs.a: Full part numbers or a precise description of each line — size, thread, pressure and material — because that is what the tariff classification is fixed from. Add the delivery estate, which decides Laem Chabang, Bangkok Port or Songkhla, and for production-line spares the make and construction currently fitted. The quotation then states the classification, Incoterm, freight mode and documents, and the invoice matches it.
